sources.title: Thomas Story Kirkbride, On the Construction, Organization, and General Arrangements of Hospitals for the Insane

facts.text: Each Kirkbride ward was to have its own dining room with a dumb waiter connected to the kitchen.
Each ward was to have an associated dormitory communicating with an attendant's chamber.
Each ward was to have single lodging rooms for patients opening off a corridor.
The Kirkbride approach held that pleasant, home-like surroundings supported recovery.
